summary.text: A two-year-old girl with a known secundum atrial septal defect and a solitary right kidney presented after three days of rhinorrhea, one day of fatigue and acute respiratory distress. In the emergency department her temperature was 100.4°F and heart rate 158/minute, with periorbital edema, tachypnea with retractions, hepatomegaly and a systolic murmur. Admission tests showed mildly elevated BUN, anion gap and NT-proBNP, and echocardiography showed a large pericardial effusion.

She was admitted to the PICU and underwent urgent pericardiocentesis. Her hemodynamics kept declining, requiring epinephrine, milrinone and calcium infusions, and LVEF fell from 66.4% to 48% within eight hours of admission. She was started on methylprednisolone and IVIG for presumed myocarditis, then intubated with femoral lines after lactate rose, and developed progressive cardiogenic shock and multiorgan failure.

Before cannulation could start she had bradycardia progressing to cardiac arrest, and ECLS was started via femoral cannulation during 27 minutes of CPR. A distal reperfusion cannula could not be placed. Afterward troponin was 33,521 ng/L and echocardiography showed myocardial stunning and two thrombi, treated with TPA at 0.03 mg/kg/hour for 12 hours and a switch from heparin to bivalirudin for suspected HIT, later excluded; the thrombi resolved with an LVSF of 4%.

Right lower extremity ischemia progressed to compartment syndrome with creatine kinase 202,830 U/L and required fasciotomy, and CRRT was started. She was transferred on ECLS for transplant evaluation, was decannulated over 20 days, and had an episode of altered mental status with a clotted CRRT circuit, with brain MRI/MRA showing an infarction and microhemorrhages. Renal function recovered after seven weeks of CRRT, and RLE osteomyelitis and foot gangrene later required a Syme amputation.

She was discharged home with a reassuring neurodevelopmental examination, and heart failure medications were weaned as biventricular function normalized. About eight months later she developed left foot drop and ankle contracture, later a left cavovarus deformity, and her ASD was closed percutaneously twenty months after the AFM. Currently she is eight years old with reassuring neurodevelopmental and cognitive assessments.
